Sometimes we will also just use the term ‘layer’ when we do not need to be precise or big vs small is clear from context. A BN big layer
f_{l}=(f_{l,1},..,f_{l,B})
takes in all values in
(f_{k,1},..,f_{k,B})
and applies the BN operation. All other big layers apply their operation batch index-wise. The small layers form a small layer graph. All small layers except BN small layers are only dependent on other small layers with the same batch index, whereas a BN small layer
f_{l,b}
is dependent on
B
small layers with varying batch index but only a single big layer index
k
. Quantities associated with big layers, such as weight matrices
W_{l}
, bias vectors
\beta_{l}
, regularization parameters
\epsilon_{l}
, activation functions
\tau_{l}
and addition weights
w_{l,\kappa_{l}}
, are shared across batch indices.

We further overload our notation by letting
X
refer to the vector that is obtained by concatenating the individual inputs in
X
and letting
f_{l}
refer to the function that is obtained by concatenating the outputs of the
f_{l,b}
. Based on this, we write
\mathcal{J}_{l,m}=\frac{df_{l}}{df_{m}}
for the derivative of one big layer with respect to another, which is a matrix of size
Bd_{l}^{\text{MF}}\times Bd_{m}^{\text{MF}}
. We write
\mathcal{J}_{l,m,b}=\frac{df_{l,b}}{df_{m}}
for the derivative of a small layer with respect to a big layer.

The properties of A-architectures given in section
5.3.1
generalize to the BN case by (i) having terms such as
d_{0}
and
d_{l}d_{\text{MF}}
refer to the width of small layers and (ii) considering that
f
has a single input and output big layer but
B
input and output small layers and (iii) replacing the phrase “layer graph” with “big layer graph”. For example, an A-architecture may contain two consecutive BN big layers even though this would violate property
22.11
if we considered the small layer graph instead.

Since mean field architectures have no BN layers and are naturally capable of having multiple input and output layers, we do not have to change our definition of them to accommodate the BN case. We will only tweak our notation slightly as will become clear in the proof of section
11.6.3
.

Given these definitions, all other NTCs used throughout the remainder of this chapter are either identical to or canonical generalizations of the corresponding concepts from earlier in this chapter.

11.6.2
Lemma

Lemma 18
.

Let …

•

…
G
and
H
be functions
\mathbb{R}^{d_{G}}\rightarrow\mathbb{R}
.

•

…
(\chi)_{d}
be a sequence of
d_{G}
-dimensional random vectors where
\chi_{d}\sim\mathcal{N}(0,\Sigma_{d})
for some
\Sigma_{d}
.

•

…
\hat{\chi}
be a
d_{G}
-dimensional random vector where
\hat{\chi}\sim\mathcal{N}(0,\hat{\Sigma})

•

…
(\omega^{G})_{d}
and
(\omega^{H})_{d}
be sequences of
d_{G}
-dimensional random vectors.

Assume:

•

\hat{\Sigma}
is positive definite.

•

\Sigma_{d}\rightarrow\hat{\Sigma}
as
d\rightarrow\infty
.

•

There exists a
B>0
such that for all
d
, the components of
\omega_{d}^{G}
and
\omega_{d}^{H}
have absolute value less than
B
.

•

\omega_{d}^{G}
and
\omega_{d}^{H}
converge almost surely to some vectors
\hat{\omega}^{G}
and
\hat{\omega}^{H}
elementwise as
d\rightarrow\infty
.

•

G
and
H
are differentiable

•

G
,
G^{\text{max}}(\chi)=\max_{\chi^{\prime}:||\chi^{\prime}||_{2}\leq||\chi||_{2}}|G(\chi^{\prime})|
,
G^{\text{maxg}}(\chi)=\max_{\chi^{\prime}:||\chi^{\prime}||_{2}\leq||\chi||_{2}}\Big|\Big|\frac{dG(\chi^{\prime})}{d\chi}\Big|\Big|_{2}
,
H
,
H^{\text{max}}
,
H^{\text{maxg}}
,
G^{\text{max}}H^{\text{max}}
,
||\chi||_{2}G^{\text{maxg}}H^{\text{max}}
,
||\chi||_{2}G^{\text{max}}H^{\text{maxg}}
,
||\chi||_{2}^{2}G^{\text{maxg}}H^{\text{maxg}}
and
G^{\text{combo}}(\chi)=G(\hat{\omega}^{G}.\chi)H(\hat{\omega}^{H}.\chi)
are integrable with respect to any Gaussian measure.

Then

\lim_{d\rightarrow\infty}\mathbb{E}G(\omega^{G}_{d}.\chi_{d})H(\omega^{H}_{d}.\chi_{d})=\mathbb{E}G(\hat{\omega}^{G}.\hat{\chi})H(\hat{\omega}^{H}.\hat{\chi})

where the expectation is taken jointly over all random vectors that occur in the expression and
\mathsf{vec1}.\mathsf{vec2}
denotes the elementwise product of two vectors as usual.

Proof.

We argue by contradiction. Assume there is an
\epsilon
such that
|\mathbb{E}G(\omega^{G}_{d}.\chi_{d})H(\omega^{H}_{d}.\chi_{d})-\mathbb{E}G(\hat{\omega}^{G}.\hat{\chi})H(\hat{\omega}^{H}.\hat{\chi})|>\epsilon
for arbitrarily large
d
. Let
B_{2}
be 1 or the largest absolute value among components in either
\hat{\omega}^{G}
or
\hat{\omega}^{H}
, whichever is larger. Then for any
d
and
0<\delta<B_{2}
we have

\displaystyle|\mathbb{E}G(\omega^{G}_{d}.\chi_{d})H(\omega^{H}_{d}.\chi_{d})-\mathbb{E}G(\hat{\omega}^{G}.\hat{\chi})H(\hat{\omega}^{H}.\hat{\chi})|

\displaystyle\leq

\displaystyle|\mathbb{E}G(\omega^{G}_{d}.\chi_{d})H(\omega^{H}_{d}.\chi_{d})-\mathbb{E}G(\hat{\omega}^{G}.\chi_{d})H(\hat{\omega}^{H}.\chi_{d})|

\displaystyle+|\mathbb{E}G(\hat{\omega}^{G}.\chi_{d})H(\hat{\omega}^{H}.\chi_{d})-\mathbb{E}G(\hat{\omega}^{G}.\hat{\chi})H(\hat{\omega}^{H}.\hat{\chi})|

\displaystyle\leq

\displaystyle\Big|\int_{|\omega^{G}_{d}[i]-\hat{\omega}^{G}[i]|<\delta\text{ and }|\omega^{H}_{d}[i]-\hat{\omega}^{H}[i]|<\delta\text{ for all $i$}}G(\omega^{G}_{d}.\chi_{d})H(\omega^{H}_{d}.\chi_{d})-G(\hat{\omega}^{G}.\chi_{d})H(\hat{\omega}^{H}.\chi_{d})d\mu\Big|

\displaystyle+\Big|\int_{|\omega^{G}_{d}[i]-\hat{\omega}^{G}[i]|\geq\delta\text{ or }|\omega^{H}_{d}[i]-\hat{\omega}^{H}[i]|\geq\delta\text{ for some $i$}}G(\omega^{G}_{d}.\chi_{d})H(\omega^{H}_{d}.\chi_{d})

\displaystyle-G(\hat{\omega}^{G}.\chi_{d})H(\hat{\omega}^{H}.\chi_{d})d\mu\Big|+|\mathbb{E}G(\hat{\omega}^{G}.\chi_{d})H(\hat{\omega}^{H}.\chi_{d})-\mathbb{E}G(\hat{\omega}^{G}.\hat{\chi})H(\hat{\omega}^{H}.\hat{\chi})|

d\mu
here is the joint measure of all random vectors.
i
ranges over all components of the
\omega
. We will address each of the three terms in turn.

First term
: Denote the
d_{G}
-dimensional gradient of
G
/
H
by
G^{\prime}
/
H^{\prime}
. Let
\chi^{\text{max}}\sim\mathcal{N}(0,sI)
be a
d_{G}
-dimensional Gaussian vector, where
s
is a positive constant larger than any eigenvalue of any of the
\Sigma_{d}
or
\hat{\Sigma}
.
s
exists because
\Sigma_{d}
converges. Using the Taylor expansion and the Lagrange form of the remainder, we have, for some (random)
\chi^{\text{inter-G}}
on the line segment between
\hat{\omega}^{G}.\chi_{d}
and
\omega^{G}_{d}.\chi_{d}
and some (random)
\chi^{\text{inter-H}}
on the line segment between
\hat{\omega}^{H}.\chi_{d}
and
\omega^{H}_{d}.\chi_{d}
, the following.

\displaystyle\Big|\int_{|\omega^{G}_{d}[i]-\hat{\omega}^{G}[i]|<\delta\text{ and }|\omega^{H}_{d}[i]-\hat{\omega}^{H}[i]|<\delta\text{ for all $i$}}G(\omega^{G}_{d}.\chi_{d})H(\omega^{H}_{d}.\chi_{d})-G(\hat{\omega}^{G}.\chi_{d})H(\hat{\omega}^{H}.\chi_{d})d\mu\Big|

\displaystyle=

\displaystyle\Big|\int_{...}G(\hat{\omega}^{G}.\chi_{d}+(\omega^{G}_{d}-\hat{\omega}^{G}).\chi_{d})H(\hat{\omega}^{H}.\chi_{d}+(\omega^{H}_{d}-\hat{\omega}^{H}).\chi_{d})-G(\hat{\omega}^{G}.\chi_{d})H(\hat{\omega}^{H}.\chi_{d})d\mu\Big|

\displaystyle=

\displaystyle\Big|\int_{...}\Big(G(\hat{\omega}^{G}.\chi_{d})+\sum_{i}\big((\omega_{d}^{G}-\hat{\omega}^{G}).\chi_{d}.G^{\prime}(\chi^{\text{inter-G}})\big)[i]\Big)...

\displaystyle...\Big(H(\hat{\omega}^{H}.\chi_{d})+\sum_{i}\big((\omega^{H}_{d}-\hat{\omega}^{H}).\chi_{d}.H^{\prime}(\chi^{\text{inter-H}})\big)[i]\Big)

\displaystyle-G(\hat{\omega}^{G}.\chi_{d})H(\hat{\omega}^{H}.\chi_{d})d\mu\Big|

\displaystyle=

\displaystyle\Big|\int_{...}\sum_{i}\big((\omega_{d}^{G}-\hat{\omega}^{G}).\chi_{d}.G^{\prime}(\chi^{\text{inter-G}})\big)[i]H(\hat{\omega}^{H}.\chi_{d})

\displaystyle+\sum_{i}\big((\omega^{H}_{d}-\hat{\omega}^{H}).\chi_{d}.H^{\prime}(\chi^{\text{inter-H}})\big)[i]G(\hat{\omega}^{G}.\chi_{d})

\displaystyle+\sum_{i}\big((\omega_{d}^{G}-\hat{\omega}^{G}).\chi_{d}.G^{\prime}(\chi^{\text{inter-G}})\big)[i]\sum_{i}\big((\omega^{H}_{d}-\hat{\omega}^{H}).\chi_{d}.H^{\prime}(\chi^{\text{inter-H}})\big)[i]d\mu\Big|

\displaystyle\leq

\displaystyle\int_{...}||(\omega^{G}_{d}-\hat{\omega}^{G}).\chi_{d}||_{2}||G^{\prime}(\chi^{\text{inter-G}})||_{2}|H(\hat{\omega}^{H}.\chi_{d})|

\displaystyle+||(\omega^{H}_{d}-\hat{\omega}^{H}).\chi_{d}||_{2}||H^{\prime}(\chi^{\text{inter-H}})||_{2}|G(\hat{\omega}^{G}.\chi_{d})|

\displaystyle+||(\omega^{G}_{d}-\hat{\omega}^{G}).\chi_{d}||_{2}||G^{\prime}(\chi^{\text{inter-G}})||_{2}||(\omega^{H}_{d}-\hat{\omega}^{H}).\chi_{d}||_{2}||H^{\prime}(\chi^{\text{inter-H}})||_{2}d\mu

\displaystyle\leq

\displaystyle\int_{...}||(\omega_{d}^{G}-\hat{\omega}^{G}).\chi_{d}||_{2}G^{\text{maxg}}(\chi^{\text{inter-G}})H^{\text{max}}(\hat{\omega}^{H}.\chi_{d})

\displaystyle+||(\omega_{d}^{H}-\hat{\omega}^{H}).\chi_{d}||_{2}H^{\text{maxg}}(\chi^{\text{inter-H}})G^{\text{max}}(\hat{\omega}^{G}.\chi_{d})

\displaystyle+||(\omega_{d}^{G}-\hat{\omega}^{G}).\chi_{d}||_{2}G^{\text{maxg}}(\chi^{\text{inter-G}})||(\omega_{d}^{H}-\hat{\omega}^{H}).\chi_{d}||_{2}H^{\text{maxg}}(\chi^{\text{inter-H}})d\mu

\displaystyle\leq

\displaystyle\int_{...}\big|\big||\omega^{G}_{d}-\hat{\omega}^{G}|.|\chi_{d}|\big|\big|_{2}G^{\text{maxg}}(\max(|\hat{\omega}^{G}|,|\omega^{G}_{d}|).|\chi_{d}|)H^{\text{max}}(|\hat{\omega}^{H}|.|\chi_{d}|)

\displaystyle+\big|\big||\omega^{H}_{d}-\hat{\omega}^{H}|.|\chi_{d}|\big|\big|_{2}H^{\text{maxg}}(\max(|\hat{\omega}^{H}|,|\omega^{H}_{d}|).|\chi_{d}|)G^{\text{max}}(|\hat{\omega}^{G}|.|\chi_{d}|)

\displaystyle+\big|\big||\omega^{G}_{d}-\hat{\omega}^{G}|.|\chi_{d}|\big|\big|_{2}G^{\text{maxg}}(\max(|\hat{\omega}^{G}|,|\omega^{G}_{d}|).|\chi_{d}|)...

\displaystyle...\big|\big||\omega^{H}_{d}-\hat{\omega}^{H}|.|\chi_{d}|\big|\big|_{2}H^{\text{maxg}}(\max(|\hat{\omega}^{H}|,|\omega^{H}_{d}|).|\chi_{d}|)d\mu

\displaystyle\leq

\displaystyle\int_{...}\big|\big|2B_{2}\delta|\chi_{d}|\big|\big|_{2}G^{\text{maxg}}(2B_{2}|\chi_{d}|)H^{\text{max}}(2B_{2}|\chi_{d}|)

\displaystyle+\big|\big|2B_{2}\delta|\chi_{d}|\big|\big|_{2}H^{\text{maxg}}(2B_{2}|\chi_{d}|)G^{\text{max}}(2B_{2}|\chi_{d}|)

\displaystyle+\big|\big|2B_{2}\delta|\chi_{d}|\big|\big|_{2}G^{\text{maxg}}(2B_{2}|\chi_{d}|)\big|\big|2B_{2}\delta|\chi_{d}|\big|\big|_{2}H^{\text{maxg}}(2B_{2}|\chi_{d}|)d\mu

\displaystyle\leq

\displaystyle\delta\mathbb{E}\big|\big|2B_{2}\chi_{d}\big|\big|_{2}G^{\text{maxg}}(2B_{2}\chi_{d})H^{\text{max}}(2B_{2}\chi_{d})+\delta\mathbb{E}\big|\big|2B_{2}\chi_{d}\big|\big|_{2}H^{\text{maxg}}(2B_{2}\chi_{d})G^{\text{max}}(2B_{2}\chi_{d})

\displaystyle+\delta^{2}\mathbb{E}\big|\big|2B_{2}\chi_{d}\big|\big|_{2}^{2}G^{\text{maxg}}(2B_{2}\chi_{d})H^{\text{maxg}}(2B_{2}\chi_{d})

\displaystyle\leq

\displaystyle\delta\mathbb{E}\big|\big|2B_{2}\chi^{\text{max}}\big|\big|_{2}G^{\text{maxg}}(2B_{2}\chi^{\text{max}})H^{\text{max}}(2B_{2}\chi^{\text{max}})

\displaystyle+\delta\mathbb{E}\big|\big|2B_{2}\chi^{\text{max}}\big|\big|_{2}H^{\text{maxg}}(2B_{2}\chi^{\text{max}})G^{\text{max}}(2B_{2}\chi^{\text{max}})

\displaystyle+\delta^{2}\mathbb{E}\big|\big|2B_{2}\chi^{\text{max}}\big|\big|_{2}^{2}G^{\text{maxg}}(2B_{2}\chi^{\text{max}})H^{\text{maxg}}(2B_{2}\chi^{\text{max}})

Here, all integrals are over the same set and
\max(.,.)
is taken elementwise when applied to vector(s). Since
||\chi||_{2}G^{\text{maxg}}(\chi)H^{\text{max}}(\chi)
,
||\chi||_{2}G^{\text{max}}(\chi)H^{\text{maxg}}(\chi)
and
||\chi||_{2}^{2}G^{\text{maxg}}(\chi)H^{\text{maxg}}(\chi)
are integrable with respect to any Gaussian measure, each of the three expectations in the last line of the derivation above is indeed finite. Since the above holds for any
0<\delta<B_{2}
, we can choose
\delta
small enough so that the expression on the last line is less than
\frac{\epsilon}{3}
. Fix
\delta
to this value going forward. The key to the above derivation is that
G^{\text{max}}
,
G^{\text{maxg}}
,
H^{\text{max}}
,
H^{\text{maxg}}
and
||.||_{2}
depend only on the length of their argument in a monotonically increasing fashion. Hence, increasing the length of their argument does not reduce their value.

Second term:
Let
(r)_{d}
be a sequence of values in
\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}\cup\{\infty\}
such that the following holds. For each
d
, the probability that
|\omega^{G}_{d}[i]-\hat{\omega}^{G}[i]|\geq\delta
or
|\omega^{H}_{d}[i]-\hat{\omega}^{H}[i]|\geq\delta
for some
i
is equal to the probability that
||B\chi^{\text{max}}||_{2}
is larger than
r_{d}
. Then

\displaystyle\Big|\int_{|\omega^{G}_{d}[i]-\hat{\omega}^{G}[i]|\geq\delta\text{ or }|\omega^{H}_{d}[i]-\hat{\omega}^{H}[i]|\geq\delta\text{ for some $i$}}G(\omega^{G}_{d}.\chi_{d})H(\omega^{H}_{d}.\chi_{d})

\displaystyle-G(\hat{\omega}^{G}.\chi_{d})H(\hat{\omega}^{H}.\chi_{d})d\mu\Big|

\displaystyle\leq

\displaystyle\int_{...}|G(\omega^{G}_{d}.\chi_{d})H(\omega^{H}_{d}.\chi_{d})|+|G(\hat{\omega}^{G}.\chi_{d})H(\hat{\omega}^{H}.\chi_{d})|d\mu

\displaystyle\leq

\displaystyle\int_{...}G^{\text{max}}(\omega^{G}_{d}.\chi_{d})H^{\text{max}}(\omega^{H}_{d}.\chi_{d})+G^{\text{max}}(\hat{\omega}^{G}.\chi_{d})H^{\text{max}}(\hat{\omega}^{H}.\chi_{d})d\mu

\displaystyle\leq

\displaystyle\int_{...}G^{\text{max}}(B\chi_{d})H^{\text{max}}(B\chi_{d})+G^{\text{max}}(B\chi_{d})H^{\text{max}}(B\chi_{d})d\mu

\displaystyle\leq

\displaystyle\int_{...}G^{\text{max}}(B\chi^{\text{max}})H^{\text{max}}(B\chi^{\text{max}})+G^{\text{max}}(B\chi^{\text{max}})H^{\text{max}}(B\chi^{\text{max}})d\mu

\displaystyle=

\displaystyle 2\int_{||B\chi^{\text{max}}||_{2}>r_{d}}G^{\text{max}}(B\chi^{\text{max}})H^{\text{max}}(B\chi^{\text{max}})d\mu

Because the
\omega^{G}_{d}
and
\omega^{H}_{d}
converge almost surely elementwise, the probability that
|\omega^{G}_{d}[i]-\hat{\omega}^{G}[i]|\geq\delta
or
|\omega^{H}_{d}[i]-\hat{\omega}^{H}[i]|\geq\delta
for some
i
converges to zero. So
r_{d}
converges to infinity. Since
G^{\text{max}}H^{\text{max}}
is integrable with respect to any Gaussian measure,
\mathbb{E}G^{\text{max}}(B\chi^{\text{max}})H^{\text{max}}(B\chi^{\text{max}})
is a valid finite value. So the last line in the above derivation converges to zero.

Third term:
Both
\chi_{d}
and
\hat{\chi}
are Gaussian with mean zero and covariance matrices
\Sigma_{d}
and
\hat{\Sigma}
. The latter is positive definite. So the third term converges to zero by lemma
15
applied to
G^{\text{combo}}
as defined in the statement of this lemma.

Hence, for
d
beyond some value, both the second and third term are less than
\frac{\epsilon}{3}
each, so
|\mathbb{E}G(\omega^{G}_{d}.\chi_{d})H(\omega^{H}_{d}.\chi_{d})-\mathbb{E}G(\hat{\omega}^{G}.\hat{\chi})H(\hat{\omega}^{H}.\hat{\chi})|<\epsilon
. Contradiction.
∎

Theorem

Remark

We note that by symmetry, analogous results hold when the batch index 1 is replaced by any other batch index
b
and the batch index 2 is replaced by any
b^{\prime}\neq b
. We then also need to assume
B\geq b
and
B\geq b^{\prime}
, which is immaterial as we take the limit of
B
to infinity.

There are several ways part 2 of theorem
5
could have been framed. Instead of taking the expectations just over the batch
X
, they could be taken over
X
and
b
. For example, instead of
\lim\frac{1}{d_{l}^{\text{MF}}}||\mathbb{E}_{X}f_{l,1}(X)||^{2}_{2}=\mathfrak{c}_{l}
, we could have used
\lim\frac{1}{d_{l}^{\text{MF}}}||\mathbb{E}_{X,b}f_{l,b}(X)||^{2}_{2}=\mathfrak{c}_{l}
, where
\mathbb{E}
applied to the discrete, finite index
b
refers to the mean as usual. We could have also used big layers, which would result in e.g.
\lim\frac{1}{Bd_{l}^{\text{MF}}}||\mathbb{E}_{X}f_{l}(X)||^{2}_{2}=\mathfrak{c}_{l}
or in considering the meta-distribution of
f_{L}
. We could consider gradients with respect to small layers, which may yield e.g.
\lim\frac{1}{d_{l}^{\text{MF}}}||\frac{df_{l,b}}{df_{m,b^{\prime}}}(X^{(1)})||_{F}^{2}=\mathbbm{1}_{b=b^{\prime}}\frac{\mathfrak{g}_{l}}{\mathfrak{g}_{m}}
. All these possible choices lead to analogous results. We made the choice to frame the theorem in terms of individual small layers and gradients with respect to big layers and applied the choice consistently throughout the theorem, except for the NLC which is defined in section
4.4.4.1
for the BN case by considering big layers. Transforming one framing of the theorem into another is left as an exercise to the reader.

Proof.

The proof is a continuation of the proof of part 1 of the theorem given in section
11.5.2
. Notation, terminology and conventions continue to apply with modifications as described in section
11.6.1
. In addition, we have the following NTCs.

•

In this proof, we will add layers to a mean field architecture
F
that have the same joint distribution as the small layers in
f
. Hence, we will denote the layer that corresponds to
f_{l,b}
as
F_{l,b}
, even though
F_{l,b}
is not a small layer but a “regular layer” in the mean field architecture context. As before, we will define the layer graph of
F
simply over all legal combinations of
\mathsf{sub}
and
\mathsf{super}
for
F^{\mathsf{super}}_{\mathsf{sub}}
. We write e.g.
F_{k,b}
for the layer corresponding to
f_{k,b}
where
f_{k}
is the dependency of
f_{l}
in the big layer graph of
f
but
F_{k,b}
is not necessarily a dependency of
F_{l,b}
. We extend this notational convention as before to e.g.
\tilde{\mathfrak{m}}_{l,b}
and
\mathfrak{c}_{l,b;l,b}
defined via table
5.1
. On the other hand, the batch index is always omitted for quantities that do not depend on it, such as
\tau_{l}
or the
\mathfrak{m}_{l}
,
\mathfrak{q}_{l}
,
\mathfrak{c}_{l}
and
\mathfrak{g}_{l}
defined via table
5.3
.

•

To simplify the presentation, we usually fix a batch index
b
to 1 and a batch index
b^{\prime}\neq b
to 2. When we do this, the argument implicitly applies to all possible choices for
b
and
b^{\prime}
due to symmetry. For example, when we show that
\rho_{l,1}
is controlled, we generally show that all
\rho_{l,b}
are controlled. When we show
\mathfrak{c}_{l,1;l,2}=0
, we generally implicitly show
\mathfrak{c}_{l,b;l,b^{\prime}}=0
for all
b\neq b^{\prime}
.

•

We place two dots over any quantity to indicate its limit with respect to
N
and
B
, e.g.
\ddot{\mathfrak{c}}_{l,b;l,b}=\lim_{B\rightarrow\infty,N\rightarrow\infty}\mathfrak{c}_{l,b;l,b}
. The double dot overrides a tilde, so e.g.
\ddot{\mathfrak{m}}_{l,b}=\lim_{B\rightarrow\infty,N\rightarrow\infty}\tilde{\mathfrak{m}}_{l,b}
. We provide more details on this throughout the proof.

•

\widehat{expr}
denotes the mean over the batch index or “batch mean”, e.g.
\widehat{e_{m}e_{l}}=\mathbb{E}_{b}e_{m,b}e_{l,b}
. Note that we use a little hat when referencing quantities that arise in lemma
18
.

•

Analogous to previous stages, we can assume
\overline{x^{(n,b)}.x^{(n^{\prime},b^{\prime})}}
is equal to
q
when
n=n^{\prime}
and
b=b^{\prime}
and equal to
c
otherwise.

•

As before, we apply proposition
15
throughout the proof, but we no longer make this explicit.

•

Going forward, no layer in
F
has mean dependencies, so we only have to consider elementwise dependencies for elementwise layers and elementwise inputs for multi-activation functions. We write e.g.
\mathbb{E}_{e}\rho_{l,1}
short for
\mathbb{E}_{e}\rho_{l,1}(e)
. According to lemma H.4 from
Yang 2019
, we then also have rank stability, so we no longer have to consider this property explicitly. Further, parameter-control reduces to “simple” control.

Stage 9
: statements (
11.1
), (
11.2
) and (
11.3
)

The case
l=0
is again trivial. For
l>1
, we will construct a mean field architecture
F
which has a layer
F_{l,b}
corresponding to each
f_{l,b}
. We proceed by induction on
l
as usual. For readin, FC, bias, addition and activation big layers, we add layers to
F
and extend
\mathcal{G}
as if we were constructing the
N
-duplex
(F^{(1)},..,F^{(N)})
early in stage 4 and its associated generator, except that the
n
index is replaced by a
b
index. Distribution equality follows as in stage 4. If
f_{l}
is a BN layer, we add elementwise layers
F_{l,b}
, each with the same width as any of the
f_{l,b}
. We set

\rho_{l,b}=\frac{\rho_{k,b}-\widehat{\rho_{k}}}{\sqrt{\nu_{l}}}\text{ where }\nu_{l}=\mathbb{E}_{b^{\prime}}(\rho_{k,b^{\prime}}-\widehat{\rho_{k}})^{2}+\epsilon_{l}

The inputs of
\rho_{l,b}
are those occurring in any of the
\rho_{k,b^{\prime}}
for any
b^{\prime}
. We obtain distribution equality because
F_{k,1},..,F_{k,B}
can be transformed to
F_{l,b}
by applying
f_{l,b}(f_{k,1},..,f_{k,B})
.
\nu_{l}>0
holds as
\epsilon_{l}>0
.

It is important to note that the resulting
F
and
\mathcal{G}
are symmetric with respect to the batch index. We exploit this in our notation by setting the batch index to 1 or 2 as described above.

Now we show limits and control. From background theorem
1
and distribution equality, we will obtain
\lim_{d_{\text{MF}}\text{ a.s.}}\overline{f_{l,1}(X^{(1)})}=\tilde{\mathfrak{m}}_{l,1}
,
\lim_{d_{\text{MF}}\text{ a.s.}}\overline{f_{l,1}(X^{(1)}).f_{l,1}(X^{(1)})}=\mathfrak{c}_{l,1;l,1}
and
\lim_{d_{\text{MF}}\text{ a.s.}}\overline{f_{l,1}(X^{(1)}).f_{l,2}(X^{(1)})}=\mathfrak{c}_{l,1;l,2}
, where
\tilde{\mathfrak{m}}_{l,1}
,
\mathfrak{c}_{l,1;l,1}
and
\mathfrak{c}_{l,1;l,2}
are defined via table
5.1
. As part of the induction, we will show (i) the validity of and give calculation rules for
\ddot{\mathfrak{m}}_{l,1}
,
\ddot{\mathfrak{c}}_{l,1;l,1}
and
\ddot{\mathfrak{c}}_{l,1;l,2}
, (ii)
\mathfrak{m}_{l}=\lim_{\vec{\epsilon}}\ddot{\mathfrak{m}}_{l,1}
,
\mathfrak{q}_{l}=\lim_{\vec{\epsilon}}\ddot{\mathfrak{c}}_{l,1;l,1}
and
\mathfrak{c}_{l}=\lim_{\vec{\epsilon}}\ddot{\mathfrak{c}}_{l,1;l,2}
, where
\mathfrak{m}_{l}
,
\mathfrak{q}_{l}
and
\mathfrak{c}_{l}
are defined via table
5.3
and (iii) if there is no directed path from an activation layer to
f_{l}
not containing an FC layer,
\lim_{B\text{ a.s.}}\mathbb{E}_{b}(\rho_{l,b}-\widehat{\rho_{l}})^{2}=\ddot{\mathfrak{c}}_{l,1;l,1}-\ddot{\mathfrak{c}}_{l,1;l,2}
, where randomness in induced by
e
distributed according to table
5.1
. Finally, we show
\ddot{\mathfrak{c}}_{l,1;l,1}>\ddot{\mathfrak{c}}_{l,1;l,2}\geq 0
(“non-singularity”). Since this stage is independent of
N
, we can use
\lim_{B,N}
and
\lim_{B}
interchangeably.

Case:
f_{l}
is a readin layer.

•

Control: NA

•

Limits: From table
5.1
, we obtain
\tilde{\mathfrak{m}}_{l,1}=0
,
\mathfrak{c}_{l,1;l,1}=q\sigma_{l}^{2}
and
\mathfrak{c}_{l,1;l,2}=c\sigma_{l}^{2}
and thus
\ddot{\mathfrak{m}}_{l,1}=0
,
\ddot{\mathfrak{c}}_{l,1;l,1}=q\sigma_{l}^{2}
and
\ddot{\mathfrak{c}}_{l,1;l,2}=c\sigma_{l}^{2}
and thus
\lim_{\vec{\epsilon}}\ddot{\mathfrak{m}}_{l,1}=0
,
\lim_{\vec{\epsilon}}\ddot{\mathfrak{c}}_{l,1;l,1}=q\sigma_{l}^{2}
and
\lim_{\vec{\epsilon}}\ddot{\mathfrak{c}}_{l,1;l,2}=c\sigma_{l}^{2}
. Since
f_{l}
is fully-connected and its dependency is the input layer, table
5.3
yields
\mathfrak{m}_{l}=0
,
\mathfrak{q}_{l}=q\sigma_{l}^{2}
and
\mathfrak{c}_{l}=c\sigma_{l}^{2}
. So we have a match, as required.

We have

\displaystyle\lim_{B\text{ a.s.}}\mathbb{E}_{b}(\rho_{l,b}-\widehat{\rho_{l}})^{2}

\displaystyle=

\displaystyle\lim_{B\text{ a.s.}}\mathbb{E}_{b}(u_{l,b}-\widehat{u_{l}})^{2}\text{ where }(u_{l,1},..,u_{l,B})\sim\mathcal{N}(0,K(B,\mathfrak{c}_{l,1;l,1},\mathfrak{c}_{l,1;l,2}))

\displaystyle=

\displaystyle\lim_{B\text{ a.s.}}\frac{(B-1)(\mathfrak{c}_{l,1;l,1}-\mathfrak{c}_{l,1;l,2})}{B}\frac{1}{B-1}\sum_{b=1}^{B-1}u_{l,b}^{2}\text{ where }(u_{l,1},..,u_{l,B-1})\sim\mathcal{N}(0,I)

By the strong law of large numbers, this is equal to
\ddot{\mathfrak{c}}_{l,1;l,1}-\ddot{\mathfrak{c}}_{l,1;l,2}
as required.

•

Non-singularity:
\ddot{\mathfrak{c}}_{l,1;l,1}-\ddot{\mathfrak{c}}_{l,1;l,2}=(q-c)\sigma_{l}^{2}>0
and
\ddot{\mathfrak{c}}_{l,1;l,2}=c\sigma_{l}^{2}\geq 0

Case:
f_{l}
is a fully-connected, non-readin layer.

•

Control: NA

•

Limits: We obtain
\tilde{\mathfrak{m}}_{l,1}=0
,
\mathfrak{c}_{l,1;l,1}=\sigma_{l}^{2}\mathfrak{c}_{k,1;k,1}
and
\mathfrak{c}_{l,1;l,2}=\sigma_{l}^{2}\mathfrak{c}_{k,1;k,2}
and thus
\ddot{\mathfrak{m}}_{l,1}=0
,
\ddot{\mathfrak{c}}_{l,1;l,1}=\sigma_{l}^{2}\ddot{\mathfrak{c}}_{k,1;k,1}
and
\ddot{\mathfrak{c}}_{l,1;l,2}=\sigma_{l}^{2}\ddot{\mathfrak{c}}_{k,1;k,2}
and thus
\lim_{\vec{\epsilon}}\ddot{\mathfrak{m}}_{l,1}=0=\mathfrak{m}_{l}
,
\lim_{\vec{\epsilon}}\ddot{\mathfrak{c}}_{l,1;l,1}=\sigma_{l}^{2}\lim_{\vec{\epsilon}}\ddot{\mathfrak{c}}_{k,1;k,1}=\sigma_{l}^{2}\mathfrak{q}_{k}=\mathfrak{q}_{l}
and
\lim_{\vec{\epsilon}}\ddot{\mathfrak{c}}_{l,1;l,2}=\sigma_{l}^{2}\lim_{\vec{\epsilon}}\ddot{\mathfrak{c}}_{k,1;k,2}=\sigma_{l}^{2}\mathfrak{c}_{k}=\mathfrak{c}_{l}
. Finally,
\lim_{B\text{ a.s.}}\mathbb{E}_{b}(\rho_{l,b}-\widehat{\rho_{l}})^{2}=\ddot{\mathfrak{c}}_{l,1;l,1}-\ddot{\mathfrak{c}}_{l,1;l,2}
as for the readin layer case above.

•

Non-singularity:
\ddot{\mathfrak{c}}_{l,1;l,1}-\ddot{\mathfrak{c}}_{l,1;l,2}=\sigma_{l}^{2}(\ddot{\mathfrak{c}}_{k,1;k,1}-\ddot{\mathfrak{c}}_{k,1;k,2})>0
and
\ddot{\mathfrak{c}}_{l,1;l,2}=\sigma_{l}^{2}\ddot{\mathfrak{c}}_{k,1;k,2}\geq 0

Case:
f_{l}
is a bias layer.

•

Control: Since
\rho_{l,1}
only has an additional linear term relative to
\rho_{k,1}
, if
\rho_{k,1}
is controlled by
\mathcal{C}^{\text{E2}}
, then so is
\rho_{l,1}
.

•

Limits: We have
\tilde{\mathfrak{m}}_{l,1}=\mathbb{E}_{e}(e_{l,1}^{\text{in}}+\rho_{k,1})=\tilde{\mathfrak{m}}_{k,1}
,
\mathfrak{c}_{l,1;l,1}=\mathbb{E}_{e}(e_{l,1}^{\text{in}}+\rho_{k,1})^{2}=\mathbb{E}_{e}e_{l,1}^{\text{in}}e_{l,1}^{\text{in}}+\mathbb{E}_{e}\rho_{k,1}^{2}+2\mathbb{E}_{e}e_{l,1}^{\text{in}}\rho_{k,1}=\mathfrak{c}_{k,1;k,1}+\sigma_{l}^{2}
and
\mathfrak{c}_{l,1;l,2}=\mathbb{E}_{e}(e_{l,1}^{\text{in}}+\rho_{k,1})(e_{l,2}^{\text{in}}+\rho_{k,2})=\mathbb{E}_{e}e_{l,1}^{\text{in}}e_{l,2}^{\text{in}}+\mathbb{E}_{e}\rho_{k,1}\rho_{k,2}+\mathbb{E}_{e}e_{l,1}^{\text{in}}\rho_{k,2}+\mathbb{E}_{e}e_{l,2}^{\text{in}}\rho_{k,1}=\mathfrak{c}_{k,1;k,2}+\sigma_{l}^{2}
and thus
\ddot{\mathfrak{m}}_{l,1}=\ddot{\mathfrak{m}}_{k,1}
,
\ddot{\mathfrak{c}}_{l,1;l,1}=\ddot{\mathfrak{c}}_{k,1;k,1}+\sigma_{l}^{2}
and
\ddot{\mathfrak{c}}_{l,1;l,2}=\ddot{\mathfrak{c}}_{k,1;k,2}+\sigma_{l}^{2}
and thus
\lim_{\vec{\epsilon}}\ddot{\mathfrak{m}}_{l,1}=\lim_{\vec{\epsilon}}\ddot{\mathfrak{m}}_{k,1}=\mathfrak{m}_{k}=\mathfrak{m}_{l}
,
\lim_{\vec{\epsilon}}\ddot{\mathfrak{c}}_{l,1;l,1}=\sigma_{l}^{2}+\lim_{\vec{\epsilon}}\ddot{\mathfrak{c}}_{k,1;k,1}=\mathfrak{q}_{k}+\sigma_{l}^{2}=\mathfrak{q}_{l}
and
\lim_{\vec{\epsilon}}\ddot{\mathfrak{c}}_{l,1;l,2}=\sigma_{l}^{2}+\lim_{\vec{\epsilon}}\ddot{\mathfrak{c}}_{k,1;k,2}=\mathfrak{c}_{k}+\sigma_{l}^{2}=\mathfrak{c}_{l}
. Here we use that the
F_{l,1}^{\text{in}}
are independent of previous layers of
F
.

If there is no directed path from an activation layer to
f_{l}
not containing an FC layer, there is no directed path from an activation layer to
f_{k}
not containing an FC layer. Hence

\displaystyle\lim_{B\text{ a.s.}}\mathbb{E}_{b}(\rho_{l,b}-\widehat{\rho_{l}})^{2}

\displaystyle=

\displaystyle\lim_{B\text{ a.s.}}\mathbb{E}_{b}(\rho_{k,b}+e_{l,b}^{\text{in}}-\mathbb{E}_{b^{\prime}}(\rho_{k,b^{\prime}}+e_{l,b^{\prime}}^{\text{in}}))^{2}

\displaystyle=

\displaystyle\lim_{B\text{ a.s.}}\mathbb{E}_{b}(\rho_{k,b}-\widehat{\rho_{k}})^{2}

\displaystyle=

\displaystyle\ddot{\mathfrak{c}}_{k,1;k,1}-\ddot{\mathfrak{c}}_{k,1;k,2}

\displaystyle=

\displaystyle\ddot{\mathfrak{c}}_{l,1;l,1}-\ddot{\mathfrak{c}}_{l,1;l,2}

•

Non-singularity:
\ddot{\mathfrak{c}}_{l,1;l,1}-\ddot{\mathfrak{c}}_{l,1;l,2}=\ddot{\mathfrak{c}}_{k,1;k,1}-\ddot{\mathfrak{c}}_{k,1;k,2}>0
and
\ddot{\mathfrak{c}}_{l,1;l,2}=\ddot{\mathfrak{c}}_{k,1;k,2}+\sigma_{l}^{2}\geq 0
.

Case:
f_{l}
is a BN layer.

•

Control: We have
\widehat{\rho_{l}^{2}}=\frac{\mathbb{E}_{b}(\rho_{k,b}-\widehat{\rho_{k}})^{2}}{\mathbb{E}_{b}(\rho_{k,b}-\widehat{\rho_{k}})^{2}+\epsilon_{l}}<1
, so
\rho_{l,1}<\sqrt{B}
, so
\rho_{l,1}
is bounded, so it is controlled by
\mathcal{C}^{\text{E2}}
.

•

Limits: By symmetry, we have
\tilde{\mathfrak{m}}_{l,1}=\widehat{\tilde{\mathfrak{m}}_{l}}=\mathbb{E}_{b}\mathbb{E}_{e}\frac{\rho_{k,b}-\widehat{\rho_{k}}}{\sqrt{\mathbb{E}_{b^{\prime}}(\rho_{k,b^{\prime}}-\widehat{\rho_{k}})^{2}+\epsilon_{l}}}=\mathbb{E}_{e}\frac{\widehat{\rho_{k}}-\widehat{\rho_{k}}}{\sqrt{\mathbb{E}_{b^{\prime}}(\rho_{k,b^{\prime}}-\widehat{\rho_{k}})^{2}+\epsilon_{l}}}=0
and thus
\ddot{\mathfrak{m}}_{l,1}=0
.

As in previous stages, we consider the recursive expansion of
\rho_{l,1}
that flows backwards through the small layer graph of
f_{l}
until it hits input and / or fully-connected layers. It is easy to see that if the expansion touches a small layer via some path in the small layer graph, it touches the corresponding big layer via an analogous path in the big layer graph. Hence, by property
22.10
, the expansion cannot hit an activation layer. It yields an expression of the following form.

\rho_{l,1}=\sum_{f_{l^{\prime}}}c_{l^{\prime}}\bigg(\prod_{f_{l^{\prime\prime}}\in P_{l^{\prime},l}}\frac{1}{\sqrt{\nu_{l^{\prime\prime}}}}\bigg)(e_{l^{\prime},1}-\widehat{e_{l^{\prime}}})

Here, the sum is over input and FC big layers
f_{l^{\prime}}
from which there exists a directed path to
f_{l}
that does not contain another FC layer. Because of property
22.11
, there exists at most one such path. We refer to this path including its endpoint
f_{l}
but excluding its starting point
f_{l^{\prime}}
as
P_{l^{\prime},l}
.
c_{l^{\prime}}
is the product of addition weights on
P_{l^{\prime},l}
, i.e. it is the product of addition weights at addition layers in
P_{l^{\prime},l}
that correspond to an addition layer dependency that is also in
P_{l^{\prime},l}
or is equal to
f_{l^{\prime}}
.
c_{l^{\prime}}=1
if there are no applicable addition weights. The product
\prod_{f_{l^{\prime\prime}}\in P_{l^{\prime},l}}
is over BN layers
f_{l^{\prime\prime}}
in
P_{l^{\prime},l}
.

We now use lemma
18
to obtain the limit of the expansion. In the following, we explain how objects from this proof map onto objects used in the lemma.
B
maps onto
d
. The number of layers
f_{l^{\prime}}
summed over maps onto
d_{G}
. Each
e_{l^{\prime},1}-\widehat{e_{l^{\prime}}}
maps onto one component of
\chi_{d}
. The corresponding
c_{l^{\prime}}\prod_{f_{l^{\prime\prime}}\in P_{l^{\prime},l}}\frac{1}{\sqrt{\nu_{l^{\prime\prime}}}}
maps onto the corresponding component of
\omega^{G}_{d}
.
\Sigma_{d}
is then a diagonal matrix with diagonal entries
\frac{B-1}{B}(\mathfrak{c}_{l^{\prime},1;l^{\prime},1}-\mathfrak{c}_{l^{\prime},1;l^{\prime},2})
and
\hat{\Sigma}
is a diagonal matrix with diagonal entries
\ddot{\mathfrak{c}}_{l^{\prime},1;l^{\prime},1}-\ddot{\mathfrak{c}}_{l^{\prime},1;l^{\prime},2}
, because there is no weight sharing between big layers in
f
. To obtain
\ddot{\mathfrak{c}}_{l,1;l,1}=\lim_{B,N}\mathbb{E}_{e}\rho_{l,1}^{2}
, we set
G(\mathsf{arg})=(\sum_{i}\mathsf{arg}[i])^{2}
, where
i
ranges over the vector components as usual. We do not need to consider
H
and
\omega^{H}_{d}
and set both to constant 1.

Let’s check the conditions. Differentiability and integrability are trivial.
\hat{\Sigma}
is a diagonal matrix with positive diagonal entries and is thus positive definite, due to the non-singularity aspect of the induction.
\lim_{d}\Sigma_{d}=\hat{\Sigma}
holds by construction. Input and FC layers in
F
have an
\tilde{\mathfrak{m}}
value of zero, so
\chi_{d}
and
\hat{\chi}
have mean zero. As a bound on the components of
\omega^{G}_{d}
, we can use
\max_{f_{l^{\prime}}}c_{l^{\prime}}\prod_{f_{l^{\prime\prime}}\in P_{l^{\prime},l}}\frac{1}{\sqrt{\epsilon_{l^{\prime\prime}}}}
. The elementwise almost sure convergence of
\omega^{G}_{d}
is obtained from
\lim_{B\text{ a.s.}}\mathbb{E}_{b}(\rho_{k^{\prime\prime},b}-\widehat{\rho_{k^{\prime\prime}}})^{2}=\ddot{\mathfrak{c}}_{k^{\prime\prime},1;k^{\prime\prime},1}-\ddot{\mathfrak{c}}_{k^{\prime\prime},1;k^{\prime\prime},2}
, which is part of the induction because, by property
22.10
, there is no directed path from an activation layer to
f_{l^{\prime\prime}}
not containing an FC layer. So we have
\ddot{\nu}_{l^{\prime\prime}}=\ddot{\mathfrak{c}}_{k^{\prime\prime},1;k^{\prime\prime},1}-\ddot{\mathfrak{c}}_{k^{\prime\prime},1;k^{\prime\prime},2}+\epsilon_{l}
, which is positive by non-singularity and as
\epsilon_{l}>0
.

Applying lemma
18
yields

\ddot{\mathfrak{c}}_{l,1;l,1}=\mathbb{E}_{u}\Big(\sum_{f_{l^{\prime}}}\frac{c_{l^{\prime}}u_{l^{\prime},1}}{\prod_{f_{l^{\prime\prime}}\in P_{l^{\prime},l}}\sqrt{\ddot{\nu}_{l^{\prime\prime}}}}\Big)^{2}\text{ where }u_{l^{\prime},1}\sim\mathcal{N}(0,\ddot{\mathfrak{c}}_{l^{\prime},1;l^{\prime},1}-\ddot{\mathfrak{c}}_{l^{\prime},1;l^{\prime},2})

where the
u_{l^{\prime},1}
are also independent of each other. Hence we further have

\ddot{\mathfrak{c}}_{l,1;l,1}=\sum_{f_{l^{\prime}}}\frac{c_{l^{\prime}}^{2}(\ddot{\mathfrak{c}}_{l^{\prime},1;l^{\prime},1}-\ddot{\mathfrak{c}}_{l^{\prime},1;l^{\prime},2})}{\prod_{f_{l^{\prime\prime}}\in P_{l^{\prime},l}}\ddot{\nu}_{l^{\prime\prime}}}=\sum_{f_{l^{\prime}}}\frac{c_{l^{\prime}}^{2}(\ddot{\mathfrak{c}}_{l^{\prime},1;l^{\prime},1}-\ddot{\mathfrak{c}}_{l^{\prime},1;l^{\prime},2})}{\prod_{f_{l^{\prime\prime}}\in P_{l^{\prime},l}}\ddot{\mathfrak{c}}_{k^{\prime\prime},1;k^{\prime\prime},1}-\ddot{\mathfrak{c}}_{k^{\prime\prime},1;k^{\prime\prime},2}+\epsilon_{l}}

Let’s look at
\ddot{\mathfrak{c}}_{l,1;l,2}
. Again, we use lemma
18
. Now
d_{G}
is twice the previous value.
\chi_{d}
now has pairs of components composed of
e_{l^{\prime},1}-\widehat{e_{l^{\prime}}}
and
e_{l^{\prime},2}-\widehat{e_{l^{\prime}}}
. The
\omega^{G}_{d}
component is the same for each pair.
\Sigma_{d}
becomes a block-diagonal matrix with
2\times 2
blocks corresponding to the
f_{l^{\prime}}
, its previous diagonal entries duplicated and off-diagonal entries
-\frac{1}{B}(\mathfrak{c}_{l^{\prime},1;l^{\prime},1}-\mathfrak{c}_{l^{\prime},1;l^{\prime},2})
within each block.
\hat{\Sigma}
remains a diagonal matrix with its previous diagonal entries duplicated. Finally,
G(\mathsf{arg})=(\sum_{i\text{ odd}}\mathsf{arg}[i])(\sum_{i\text{ even}}\mathsf{arg}[i])
. We obtain
\ddot{\mathfrak{c}}_{l,1;l,2}=0
. Using this, as well as the recursive calculation rules for bias layers and addition layers (see below), it is easy to check that
\ddot{\mathfrak{c}}_{l,1;l,1}=\frac{\ddot{\mathfrak{c}}_{k,1;k,1}-\ddot{\mathfrak{c}}_{k,1;k,2}}{\ddot{\mathfrak{c}}_{k,1;k,1}-\ddot{\mathfrak{c}}_{k,1;k,2}+\epsilon_{l}}
. So
\lim_{\vec{\epsilon}}\ddot{\mathfrak{m}}_{l,1}=0=\mathfrak{m}_{l}
,
\lim_{\vec{\epsilon}}\ddot{\mathfrak{c}}_{l,1;l,2}=0=\mathfrak{c}_{l}
and
\lim_{\vec{\epsilon}}\ddot{\mathfrak{c}}_{l,1;l,1}=\lim_{\vec{\epsilon}}\frac{\ddot{\mathfrak{c}}_{k,1;k,1}-\ddot{\mathfrak{c}}_{k,1;k,2}}{\ddot{\mathfrak{c}}_{k,1;k,1}-\ddot{\mathfrak{c}}_{k,1;k,2}+\epsilon_{l}}=\frac{\lim_{\vec{\epsilon}}\ddot{\mathfrak{c}}_{k,1;k,1}-\lim_{\vec{\epsilon}}\ddot{\mathfrak{c}}_{k,1;k,2}}{\lim_{\vec{\epsilon}}\ddot{\mathfrak{c}}_{k,1;k,1}-\lim_{\vec{\epsilon}}\ddot{\mathfrak{c}}_{k,1;k,2}+\lim_{\vec{\epsilon}}\epsilon_{l}}=\frac{\mathfrak{q}_{k}-\mathfrak{c}_{k}}{\mathfrak{q}_{k}-\mathfrak{c}_{k}}=1
.

If there is no directed path from an activation layer to
f_{l}
not containing an FC layer, there is no directed path from an activation layer to
f_{k}
not containing an FC layer. Hence

\displaystyle\lim_{B\text{ a.s.}}\mathbb{E}_{b}(\rho_{l,b}-\widehat{\rho_{l}})^{2}

\displaystyle=

\displaystyle\lim_{B\text{ a.s.}}\mathbb{E}_{b}\frac{(\rho_{k,b}-\widehat{\rho_{k}}-\mathbb{E}_{b^{\prime}}(\rho_{k,b^{\prime}}-\widehat{\rho_{k}}))^{2}}{\mathbb{E}_{b}(\rho_{k,b}-\widehat{\rho_{k}})^{2}+\epsilon_{l}}

\displaystyle=

\displaystyle\frac{\lim_{B\text{ a.s.}}\mathbb{E}_{b}(\rho_{k,b}-\widehat{\rho_{k}})^{2}}{\lim_{B\text{ a.s.}}\mathbb{E}_{b}(\rho_{k,b}-\widehat{\rho_{k}})^{2}+\epsilon_{l}}

\displaystyle=

\displaystyle\frac{\ddot{\mathfrak{c}}_{k,1;k,1}-\ddot{\mathfrak{c}}_{k,1;k,2}}{\ddot{\mathfrak{c}}_{k,1;k,1}-\ddot{\mathfrak{c}}_{k,1;k,2}+\epsilon_{l}}

\displaystyle=

\displaystyle\ddot{\mathfrak{c}}_{l,1;l,1}

\displaystyle=

\displaystyle\ddot{\mathfrak{c}}_{l,1;l,1}-\ddot{\mathfrak{c}}_{l,1;l,2}

•

Non-singularity: We have
\ddot{\mathfrak{c}}_{l,1;l,1}-\ddot{\mathfrak{c}}_{l,1;l,2}=\frac{\ddot{\mathfrak{c}}_{k,1;k,1}-\ddot{\mathfrak{c}}_{k,1;k,2}}{\ddot{\mathfrak{c}}_{k,1;k,1}-\ddot{\mathfrak{c}}_{k,1;k,2}+\epsilon_{l}}>0
and
\ddot{\mathfrak{c}}_{l,1;l,2}=0\geq 0
.

Case:
f_{l}
is an addition layer.

•

Control: Since
\mathcal{C}^{\text{E2}}
is linearly closed, if the
\rho_{k[\kappa],1}
are controlled by
\mathcal{C}^{\text{E2}}
, so is
\rho_{l,1}
.

•

Limits: The argument is analogous to stage 1.
\tilde{\mathfrak{m}}_{l,1}=\mathbb{E}_{e}\sum_{\kappa=1}^{K}w_{\kappa}\rho_{k[\kappa],1}=\sum_{\kappa=1}^{K}w_{\kappa}\tilde{\mathfrak{m}}_{k[\kappa],1}
. Further,
\mathfrak{c}_{l,1;l,1}=\mathbb{E}_{e}(\sum_{\kappa=1}^{K}w_{\kappa}\rho_{k[\kappa],1})^{2}=\sum_{\kappa=1}^{K}w_{\kappa}^{2}\mathfrak{c}_{k[\kappa],1;k[\kappa],1}+\sum_{\kappa\neq\kappa^{\prime}}w_{\kappa}w_{\kappa^{\prime}}\mathbb{E}_{e}\rho_{k[\kappa],1}\rho_{k[\kappa^{\prime}],1}
. Consider some specific
\kappa\neq\kappa^{\prime}
. Due to property
22.11
, there cannot be a big layer in the big layer graph of
f
that is touched by both the recursive expansion of
\rho_{k[\kappa],1}
and
\rho_{k[\kappa^{\prime}],1}
. Hence, the dependencies of
F_{k[\kappa],1}
correspond to different big layers in
f
than the dependencies of
F_{k[\kappa^{\prime}],1}
. Since there is no weight sharing between big layers and the entries of the covariance matrix of
\mathcal{G}
corresponding to different big layers in
f
are zero by construction,
\mathfrak{c}_{l,b;m,b^{\prime}}=0
when
F_{l,b}
and
F_{m,b^{\prime}}
are FC or input layers of equal width and
l\neq m
. (Here,
F_{l,b}
or
F_{m,b^{\prime}}
may also refer to
F_{l,b}^{\text{in}}
or
F_{m,b^{\prime}}^{\text{in}}
.) Hence, we have
\mathbb{E}_{e}\rho_{k[\kappa],1}\rho_{k[\kappa^{\prime}],1}=\mathbb{E}_{e}\rho_{k[\kappa],1}\mathbb{E}_{e}\rho_{k[\kappa^{\prime}],1}=\tilde{\mathfrak{m}}_{k[\kappa],1}\tilde{\mathfrak{m}}_{k[\kappa^{\prime}],1}
. Further, by property
22.9
, the expansion of at least one of
\rho_{k[\kappa],1}
and
\rho_{k[\kappa^{\prime}],1}
does not touch an activation layer. WLOG let it be
\rho_{k[\kappa],1}
. Assume
\tilde{\mathfrak{m}}_{k[\kappa],1}\neq 0
. By the induction, we must have that
f_{k[\kappa],1}
is a bias or addition layer with a dependency that also corresponds to an
\tilde{\mathfrak{m}}
value unequal to 1. Then that dependency must also have one such dependency. This cannot continue forever. So indeed
\tilde{\mathfrak{m}}_{k[\kappa],1}=0
. So
\mathbb{E}_{e}\rho_{k[\kappa],1}\rho_{k[\kappa^{\prime}],1}=0
for any
\kappa\neq\kappa^{\prime}
, so
\mathfrak{c}_{l,1;l,1}=\sum_{\kappa=1}^{K}w_{\kappa}^{2}\mathfrak{c}_{k[\kappa],1;k[\kappa],1}
. Similarly,
\mathfrak{c}_{l,1;l,2}=\sum_{\kappa=1}^{K}w_{\kappa}^{2}\mathfrak{c}_{k[\kappa],1;k[\kappa],2}
.

Then we have
\ddot{\mathfrak{m}}_{l,1}=\sum_{\kappa=1}^{K}w_{\kappa}\ddot{\mathfrak{m}}_{k[\kappa],1}
,
\ddot{\mathfrak{c}}_{l,1;l,1}=\sum_{\kappa=1}^{K}w_{\kappa}^{2}\ddot{\mathfrak{c}}_{k[\kappa],1;k[\kappa],1}
and
\ddot{\mathfrak{c}}_{l,1;l,2}=\sum_{\kappa=1}^{K}w_{\kappa}^{2}\ddot{\mathfrak{c}}_{k[\kappa],1;k[\kappa],2}
and thus
\lim_{\vec{\epsilon}}\ddot{\mathfrak{m}}_{l,1}=\sum_{\kappa=1}^{K}w_{\kappa}\lim_{\vec{\epsilon}}\ddot{\mathfrak{m}}_{k[\kappa],1}=\sum_{\kappa=1}^{K}w_{\kappa}\mathfrak{m}_{k}=\mathfrak{m}_{l}
,
\lim_{\vec{\epsilon}}\ddot{\mathfrak{c}}_{l,1;l,1}=\sum_{\kappa=1}^{K}w_{\kappa}^{2}\lim_{\vec{\epsilon}}\ddot{\mathfrak{c}}_{k[\kappa],1;k[\kappa],1}=\sum_{\kappa=1}^{K}w_{\kappa}^{2}\mathfrak{q}_{k[\kappa]}=\mathfrak{q}_{l}
and
\lim_{\vec{\epsilon}}\ddot{\mathfrak{c}}_{l,1;l,2}=\sum_{\kappa=1}^{K}w_{\kappa}^{2}\lim_{\vec{\epsilon}}\ddot{\mathfrak{c}}_{k[\kappa],1;k[\kappa],2}=\sum_{\kappa=1}^{K}w_{\kappa}^{2}\mathfrak{c}_{k[\kappa]}=\mathfrak{c}_{l}
.

Now assume that there is no directed path from an activation layer to
f_{l}
not containing an FC layer. Then there is no directed path from an activation layer to any
f_{k[\kappa]}
not containing an FC layer. We have

\displaystyle\lim_{B\text{ a.s.}}\mathbb{E}_{b}(\rho_{l,b}-\widehat{\rho_{l}})^{2}

\displaystyle=

\displaystyle\lim_{B\text{ a.s.}}\mathbb{E}_{b}\Big(\sum_{\kappa=1}^{K}w_{\kappa}(\rho_{k[\kappa],b}-\widehat{\rho_{k[\kappa]}})\Big)^{2}

\displaystyle=

\displaystyle\sum_{\kappa}w_{\kappa}^{2}\lim_{B\text{ a.s.}}\mathbb{E}_{b}(\rho_{k[\kappa],b}-\widehat{\rho_{k[\kappa]}})^{2}

\displaystyle+\sum_{\kappa\neq\kappa^{\prime}}w_{\kappa}w_{\kappa^{\prime}}\lim_{B\text{ a.s.}}\mathbb{E}_{b}(\rho_{k[\kappa],b}-\widehat{\rho_{k[\kappa]}})(\rho_{k[\kappa^{\prime}],b}-\widehat{\rho_{k[\kappa^{\prime}]}})

The induction hypothesis yields
\lim_{B\text{ a.s.}}\mathbb{E}_{b}(\rho_{k[\kappa],b}-\widehat{\rho_{k[\kappa]}})^{2}=\ddot{\mathfrak{c}}_{k[\kappa],1;k[\kappa],1}-\ddot{\mathfrak{c}}_{k[\kappa],1;k[\kappa],2}
. Further, the recursive expansion of
\rho_{k[\kappa],1}-\widehat{\rho_{k[\kappa]}}
is as for the BN layer case above, and so for any
\kappa\neq\kappa^{\prime}

\displaystyle\lim_{B\text{ a.s.}}\mathbb{E}_{b}(\rho_{k[\kappa],b}-\widehat{\rho_{k[\kappa]}})(\rho_{k[\kappa^{\prime}],b}-\widehat{\rho_{k[\kappa^{\prime}]}})

\displaystyle=

\displaystyle\lim_{B\text{ a.s.}}\mathbb{E}_{b}\Big(\sum_{f_{l^{\prime}}}c_{l^{\prime}}\bigg(\prod_{f_{l^{\prime\prime}}\in P_{l^{\prime},l}}\frac{1}{\sqrt{\nu_{l^{\prime\prime}}}}\bigg)(e_{l^{\prime},b}-\widehat{e_{l^{\prime}}})\Big)...

\displaystyle...\Big(\sum_{f_{\lambda}}c_{\lambda}\bigg(\prod_{f_{l^{\prime\prime}}\in P_{\lambda,l}}\frac{1}{\sqrt{\nu_{l^{\prime\prime}}}}\bigg)(e_{\lambda,b}-\widehat{e_{\lambda}})\Big)

\displaystyle=

\displaystyle\sum_{f_{l^{\prime}}}\sum_{f_{\lambda}}c_{l^{\prime}}c_{\lambda}\frac{\lim_{B\text{ a.s.}}\mathbb{E}_{b}(e_{l^{\prime},b}-\widehat{e_{l^{\prime}}})(e_{\lambda,b}-\widehat{e_{\lambda}})}{\bigg(\prod_{f_{l^{\prime\prime}}\in P_{l^{\prime},l}}\frac{1}{\sqrt{\ddot{\nu}_{l^{\prime\prime}}}}\bigg)\bigg(\prod_{f_{l^{\prime\prime}}\in P_{\lambda,l}}\frac{1}{\sqrt{\ddot{\nu}_{l^{\prime\prime}}}}\bigg)}

Here,
\sum_{f_{l^{\prime}}}
is over the input and FC big layers from which there exists a directed path to
f_{k[\kappa]}
that does not contain another FC layer.
\sum_{f_{\lambda}}
is the analogous sum for
f_{k[\kappa^{\prime}]}
. Because of property
22.11
, there is no big layer that appears in both sums and so the
e_{l^{\prime},b}
are independent of the
e_{\lambda,b}
. Hence we continue the above derivation as follows.

\displaystyle=

\displaystyle\sum_{f_{l^{\prime}}}\sum_{f_{\lambda}}c_{l^{\prime}}c_{\lambda}\frac{\lim_{B\text{ a.s.}}\mathbb{E}_{b}(u_{l^{\prime},b}-\widehat{u_{l^{\prime}}})(u_{\lambda,b}-\widehat{u_{\lambda}})}{\bigg(\prod_{f_{l^{\prime\prime}}\in P_{l^{\prime},l}}\frac{1}{\sqrt{\ddot{\nu}_{l^{\prime\prime}}}}\bigg)\bigg(\prod_{f_{l^{\prime\prime}}\in P_{\lambda,l}}\frac{1}{\sqrt{\ddot{\nu}_{l^{\prime\prime}}}}\bigg)}

\displaystyle\text{where }u_{l^{\prime},b}\sim\mathcal{N}(0,\mathfrak{c}_{l^{\prime},1;l^{\prime},1}-\mathfrak{c}_{l^{\prime},1;l^{\prime},2}),u_{\lambda,b}\sim\mathcal{N}(0,\mathfrak{c}_{\lambda,1;\lambda,1}-\mathfrak{c}_{\lambda,1;\lambda,2})

\displaystyle\text{for }1\leq b\leq B

\displaystyle=

\displaystyle\sum_{f_{l^{\prime}}}\sum_{f_{\lambda}}c_{l^{\prime}}c_{\lambda}\frac{\lim_{B\text{ a.s.}}\widehat{u_{l^{\prime}}u_{\lambda}}-\lim_{B\text{ a.s.}}\widehat{u_{l^{\prime}}}\lim_{B\text{ a.s.}}\widehat{u_{\lambda}}}{\bigg(\prod_{f_{l^{\prime\prime}}\in P_{l^{\prime},l}}\frac{1}{\sqrt{\ddot{\nu}_{l^{\prime\prime}}}}\bigg)\bigg(\prod_{f_{l^{\prime\prime}}\in P_{\lambda,l}}\frac{1}{\sqrt{\ddot{\nu}_{l^{\prime\prime}}}}\bigg)}

By the strong law of large numbers, all three limits are zero, so
\lim_{B\text{ a.s.}}\mathbb{E}_{b}(\rho_{k[\kappa],b}-\widehat{\rho_{k[\kappa]}})(\rho_{k[\kappa^{\prime}],b}-\widehat{\rho_{k[\kappa^{\prime}]}})=0
, so
\lim_{B\text{ a.s.}}\mathbb{E}_{b}(\rho_{l,b}-\widehat{\rho_{l}})^{2}=\sum_{\kappa=1}^{K}w_{\kappa}^{2}(\ddot{\mathfrak{c}}_{k[\kappa],1;k[\kappa],1}-\ddot{\mathfrak{c}}_{k[\kappa],1;k[\kappa],2})=\ddot{\mathfrak{c}}_{l,1;l,1}-\ddot{\mathfrak{c}}_{l,1;l,2}
as required.

•

Non-singularity: As the addition weights are non-zero, we have
\ddot{\mathfrak{c}}_{l,1;l,1}-\ddot{\mathfrak{c}}_{l,1;l,2}=\sum_{\kappa}w_{\kappa}^{2}(\ddot{\mathfrak{c}}_{k[\kappa],1;k[\kappa],1}-\ddot{\mathfrak{c}}_{k[\kappa],1;k[\kappa],2})>0
and
\ddot{\mathfrak{c}}_{l,1;l,2}=\sum_{\kappa}w_{\kappa}^{2}\ddot{\mathfrak{c}}_{k[\kappa],1;k[\kappa],2}\geq 0
.

Case:
f_{l}
is an activation layer.

•

Control: The recursive expansion yields the following form for
\rho_{l,1}
.

\rho_{l,1}=\tau_{l}(\rho_{k,1})=\tau_{l}\Bigg(\sum_{f_{l^{\prime}}\text{ normed}}c_{l^{\prime}}\bigg(\prod_{f_{l^{\prime\prime}}\in P_{l^{\prime},l}}\frac{1}{\sqrt{\nu_{l^{\prime\prime}}}}\bigg)(e_{l^{\prime},1}-\widehat{e_{l^{\prime}}})+\sum_{f_{l^{\prime}}\text{ unnormed}}c_{l^{\prime}}e_{l^{\prime},1}+\sum_{f_{l^{\prime}}\text{ bias}}c_{l^{\prime}}e_{l^{\prime},1}^{\text{in}}\Bigg)

The first sum is the same as for the BN layer case above, except that it is restricted to FC and input big layers for which
P_{l^{\prime},l}
contains a BN big layer. The second sum is over FC and input big layers for which
P_{l^{\prime},l}
exists and does not contain a BN layer and the third sum is over bias layers for which
P_{l^{\prime},l}
exists and does not contain a BN layer and for which
\sigma_{l^{\prime}}^{2}>0
. The
c_{l^{\prime}}
are the products of addition weights as before, which are equal to 1 if there is no addition layer in
P_{l^{\prime},l}
.

The
\nu_{l^{\prime\prime}}
are bounded below by
\epsilon_{l^{\prime\prime}}
. Hence,
\rho_{k,1}
is controlled by
\mathcal{C}^{1}
.
\tau_{l}
is controlled by
\mathcal{C}^{\text{E2}}
by property
22.2
. So
\tau_{l}(\rho_{k,1})\leq\tau_{l}(c||e||_{2}+c^{\prime})\leq e^{(c||e||_{2}+c^{\prime})^{2-c^{\prime\prime}}+c^{\prime\prime\prime}}
for some
c,c^{\prime},c^{\prime\prime},c^{\prime\prime\prime}>0
, which is controlled by
\mathcal{C}^{\text{E2}}
.

•

Limits: We’ll apply lemma
18
five times: (i) on
\mathbb{E}_{e}\rho_{k,1}^{2}
, (ii) on
\mathbb{E}_{e}\rho_{k,1}\rho_{k,2}
, (iii) on
\mathbb{E}_{e}\rho_{l,1}
, (iv) on
\mathbb{E}_{e}\rho_{l,1}^{2}
and (v) on
\mathbb{E}_{e}\rho_{l,1}\rho_{l,2}
. The first two are analogous to the BN layer case above and yield

\ddot{\mathfrak{c}}_{k,1;k,1}=\mathbb{E}_{u}\Big(\sum_{f_{l^{\prime}}\text{ normed}}\frac{c_{l^{\prime}}u_{l^{\prime},1}}{\prod_{f_{l^{\prime\prime}}\in P_{l^{\prime},l}}\sqrt{\ddot{\nu}_{l^{\prime\prime}}}}+\sum_{f_{l^{\prime}}\text{ unnormed}}c_{l^{\prime}}u_{l^{\prime},1}+\sum_{f_{l^{\prime}}\text{ bias}}c_{l^{\prime}}u_{l^{\prime}}^{\text{in}}\Big)^{2}

\text{ where }\begin{cases}u_{l^{\prime},1}\sim\mathcal{N}(0,\ddot{\mathfrak{c}}_{l^{\prime},1;l^{\prime},1}-\ddot{\mathfrak{c}}_{l^{\prime},1;l^{\prime},2})\text{ for sum 1}\\
u_{l^{\prime},1}\sim\mathcal{N}(0,\ddot{\mathfrak{c}}_{l^{\prime},1;l^{\prime},1})\text{ for sum 2}\\
u_{l^{\prime}}^{\text{in}}\sim\mathcal{N}(0,\sigma_{l^{\prime}}^{2})\text{ for sum 3}\end{cases}

and

\ddot{\mathfrak{c}}_{k,1;k,2}=\mathbb{E}_{u}\Bigg(\Big(\sum_{f_{l^{\prime}}\text{ normed}}\frac{c_{l^{\prime}}u_{l^{\prime},1}}{\prod_{f_{l^{\prime\prime}}\in P_{l^{\prime},l}}\sqrt{\ddot{\nu}_{l^{\prime\prime}}}}+\sum_{f_{l^{\prime}}\text{ unnormed}}c_{l^{\prime}}u_{l^{\prime},1}+\sum_{f_{l^{\prime}}\text{ bias}}c_{l^{\prime}}u_{l^{\prime}}^{\text{in}}\Big)...

...\Big(\sum_{f_{l^{\prime}}\text{ normed}}\frac{c_{l^{\prime}}u_{l^{\prime},2}}{\prod_{f_{l^{\prime\prime}}\in P_{l^{\prime},l}}\sqrt{\ddot{\nu}_{l^{\prime\prime}}}}+\sum_{f_{l^{\prime}}\text{ unnormed}}c_{l^{\prime}}u_{l^{\prime},2}+\sum_{f_{l^{\prime}}\text{ bias}}c_{l^{\prime}}u_{l^{\prime}}^{\text{in}}\Big)\Bigg)

\text{ where }\begin{cases}u_{l^{\prime},1},u_{l^{\prime},2}\sim\mathcal{N}\Bigg(0,\begin{pmatrix}\ddot{\mathfrak{c}}_{l^{\prime},1;l^{\prime},1}-\ddot{\mathfrak{c}}_{l^{\prime},1;l^{\prime},2}&0\\
0&\ddot{\mathfrak{c}}_{l^{\prime},1;l^{\prime},1}-\ddot{\mathfrak{c}}_{l^{\prime},1;l^{\prime},2}\end{pmatrix}\Bigg)\text{ for sum 1}\\
u_{l^{\prime},1},u_{l^{\prime},2}\sim\mathcal{N}\Bigg(0,\begin{pmatrix}\ddot{\mathfrak{c}}_{l^{\prime},1;l^{\prime},1}&\ddot{\mathfrak{c}}_{l^{\prime},1;l^{\prime},2}\\
\ddot{\mathfrak{c}}_{l^{\prime},1;l^{\prime},2}&\ddot{\mathfrak{c}}_{l^{\prime},1;l^{\prime},1}\end{pmatrix}\Bigg)\text{ for sum 2}\\
u_{l^{\prime}}^{\text{in}}\sim\mathcal{N}(0,\sigma_{l^{\prime}}^{2})\text{ for sum 3}\end{cases}

Again, the components of
\chi_{d}
and
\hat{\chi}
correspond to the different
u
terms. By non-singularity,
\hat{\Sigma}
is positive definite. For (ii), note that the
u_{l^{\prime}}^{\text{in}}
do not depend on the batch index. Because
e_{l^{\prime},b}^{\text{in}}
takes the same value for each batch index, all the
e_{l^{\prime},b}^{\text{in}}
are represented by a single component of
\chi_{d}
/
\omega_{d}^{G}
. So
G(\mathsf{arg})
becomes
(\sum_{i\text{ odd or bias}}\mathsf{arg}[i])(\sum_{i\text{ even or bias}}\mathsf{arg}[i])
. (iii) and (vi) are analogous to the setup of (i) where
G(\mathsf{arg})=\tau_{l}(\sum_{i}\mathsf{arg}[i])
and
G(\mathsf{arg})=\tau_{l}(\sum_{i}\mathsf{arg}[i])^{2}
respectively. Differentiability follows from property
22.2
and integrability from assumption
6
. This yields
\ddot{\mathfrak{m}}_{l,1}=\mathbb{E}_{u}\tau_{l}(...)
and
\ddot{\mathfrak{c}}_{l,1;l,1}=\mathbb{E}_{u}\tau_{l}(...)^{2}
where the expression inside the parentheses is an in (i) above. Because that expression is a linear combination of zero mean Gaussians, we can combine the above results to obtain
\ddot{\mathfrak{m}}_{l,1}=\mathbb{E}_{s\sim\mathcal{N}(0,\ddot{\mathfrak{c}}_{k,1;k,1})}\tau_{l}(s)
and
\ddot{\mathfrak{c}}_{l,1;l,1}=\mathbb{E}_{s\sim\mathcal{N}(0,\ddot{\mathfrak{c}}_{k,1;k,1})}\tau_{l}(s)^{2}=\mathfrak{C}_{\tau_{l}}(\ddot{\mathfrak{c}}_{k,1;k,1},\ddot{\mathfrak{c}}_{k,1;k,1})
.

Finally, for (v) we use the setup of (ii) with
G(\mathsf{arg})=\tau_{l}(\sum_{i\text{ odd or bias}}\mathsf{arg}[i])\tau_{l}(\sum_{i\text{ even or bias}}\mathsf{arg}[i])
. This yields the same result as in (ii) except that
\tau_{l}
is applied to each of the two large parentheses. Combining this with previous results, we obtain
\ddot{\mathfrak{c}}_{l,1;l,2}=\mathfrak{C}_{\tau_{l}}(\ddot{\mathfrak{c}}_{k,1;k,1},\ddot{\mathfrak{c}}_{k,1;k,2})
. Finally, by lemma
15
, we have
\lim_{\vec{\epsilon}}\ddot{\mathfrak{m}}_{l,1}=\mathbb{E}_{s\sim\mathcal{N}(0,\mathfrak{q}_{k})}\tau_{l}(s)=\mathfrak{m}_{l}
,
\lim_{\vec{\epsilon}}\ddot{\mathfrak{c}}_{l,1;l,1}=\mathfrak{C}_{\tau_{l}}(\mathfrak{q}_{k},\mathfrak{q}_{k})=\mathfrak{q}_{l}
and
\lim_{\vec{\epsilon}}\ddot{\mathfrak{c}}_{l,1;l,2}=\mathfrak{C}_{\tau_{l}}(\mathfrak{q}_{k},\mathfrak{c}_{k})=\mathfrak{c}_{l}
as required.

Because the path containing just
f_{l}
is a directed path from an activation layer to
f_{l}
,
\lim_{B\text{ a.s.}}\mathbb{E}_{b}(\rho_{l,b}-\widehat{\rho_{l}})^{2}
is immaterial.

•

Non-singularity: We have
\ddot{\mathfrak{c}}_{l,1;l,1}-\ddot{\mathfrak{c}}_{l,1;l,2}=\mathfrak{C}_{\tau_{l}}(\ddot{\mathfrak{c}}_{k,1;k,1},\ddot{\mathfrak{c}}_{k,1;k,1})-\mathfrak{C}_{\tau_{l}}(\ddot{\mathfrak{c}}_{k,1;k,1},\ddot{\mathfrak{c}}_{k,1;k,2})>0
by proposition
12
and
\ddot{\mathfrak{c}}_{l,1;l,2}=\mathfrak{C}_{\tau_{l}}(\ddot{\mathfrak{c}}_{k,1;k,1},\ddot{\mathfrak{c}}_{k,1;k,2})\geq 0
by proposition
13
.

Stage 10
: statement (
11.4
)

We proceed along the lines of stage 2. The statement trivially holds for
l=0
. For
l>0
, we consider the 2-duplex of the architecture constructed for stage 9, where we write
F^{\prime}
and
F^{\prime\prime}
for the sub-architectures as in stage 2.
\mathcal{G}
is as in stage 4, except that there are
2B
instead of
N
components for each
f_{l}
. It is Gaussian with mean zero and a covariance matrix as follows. An entry corresponding to layers
F_{l,b}^{\mathsf{prime1}}
and
F_{l^{\prime},b^{\prime}}^{\mathsf{prime2}}
deriving from readin layers is 0 if
l\neq l^{\prime}
;
q\sigma_{l}^{2}
if
l=l^{\prime}
,
b=b^{\prime}
and
\mathsf{prime1}=\mathsf{prime2}
; and
c\sigma_{l}^{2}
otherwise. An entry corresponding to
F_{l,b}^{\mathsf{prime1}\text{ in}}
and
F_{l^{\prime},b^{\prime}}^{\mathsf{prime2}\text{ in}}

l\neq l^{\prime}
and
\sigma_{l}^{2}
otherwise. An entry corresponding to
F_{l,b}^{\mathsf{prime1}}
and
F_{l^{\prime},b^{\prime}}^{\mathsf{prime2}\text{ in}}
is zero.
\mathsf{prime1}
and
\mathsf{prime2}
stand for
′
or
′′
. Distribution equality follows as before. Control follows from stage 9. What remains is to investigate the limits. As in stage 9,
F
and
\mathcal{G}
are symmetric with respect to the batch index. Specifically, the joint distribution of
\rho_{l,b}^{\prime}
and
\rho_{l,b^{\prime}}^{\prime\prime}
is independent of both
b
and
b^{\prime}
, so it is enough to investigate e.g.
\mathbb{E}_{e}\rho_{l,1}^{\prime}\rho_{l,1}^{\prime\prime}
, which is the same as e.g.
\mathbb{E}_{e}\rho_{l,1}^{\prime}\rho_{l,2}^{\prime\prime}
. We have
\mathfrak{c}^{\prime;\prime}_{l,1;l,1}=\mathfrak{c}^{\prime\prime;\prime\prime}_{l,1;l,1}=\mathfrak{c}_{l,1;l,1}
, where the value of
\ddot{\mathfrak{c}}_{l,1;l,1}
carries over from the mean field architecture constructed in stage 9 for the same
f
. The induction below will show
\ddot{\mathfrak{c}}^{\prime;\prime\prime}_{l,1;l,1}=\ddot{\mathfrak{c}}_{l,1;l,2}
. This automatically yields
\ddot{\mathfrak{c}}^{\prime;\prime}_{l,1;l,1}-\ddot{\mathfrak{c}}^{\prime;\prime\prime}_{l,1;l,1}=\ddot{\mathfrak{c}}^{\prime\prime;\prime\prime}_{l,1;l,1}-\ddot{\mathfrak{c}}^{\prime;\prime\prime}_{l,1;l,1}>0
and
\ddot{\mathfrak{c}}^{\prime;\prime\prime}_{l,1;l,1}\geq 0
, i.e. non-singularity, as well as
\lim_{\vec{\epsilon}}\ddot{\mathfrak{c}}^{\prime;\prime\prime}_{l,1;l,1}=\mathfrak{c}_{l}
. Like stage 9, this stage is independent of
N
so we can use
\lim_{B,N}
and
\lim_{B}
interchangeably.

•

Case:
f_{l}
is a readin layer. From table
5.1
, we obtain
\mathfrak{c}^{\prime;\prime\prime}_{l,1;l,1}=c\sigma_{l}^{2}
and so
\ddot{\mathfrak{c}}^{\prime;\prime\prime}_{l,1;l,1}=c\sigma_{l}^{2}=\ddot{\mathfrak{c}}_{l,1;l,2}
.

•

Case:
f_{l}
is a fully-connected, non-readin layer.
\mathfrak{c}^{\prime;\prime\prime}_{l,1;l,1}=\sigma_{l}^{2}\mathfrak{c}^{\prime;\prime\prime}_{k,1;k,1}
, and so
\ddot{\mathfrak{c}}^{\prime;\prime\prime}_{l,1;l,1}=\sigma_{l}^{2}\ddot{\mathfrak{c}}^{\prime;\prime\prime}_{k,1;k,1}=\sigma_{l}^{2}\ddot{\mathfrak{c}}_{k,1;k,2}=\ddot{\mathfrak{c}}_{l,1;l,2}
.

•

Case:
f_{l}
is a bias layer. We have
\mathfrak{c}^{\prime;\prime\prime}_{l,1;l,1}=\mathbb{E}_{e}(e_{l,1}^{\prime\text{in}}+\rho_{k,1}^{\prime})(e_{l,1}^{\prime\prime\text{in}}+\rho_{k,1}^{\prime\prime})=\mathfrak{c}^{\prime;\prime\prime}_{k,1;k,1}+\sigma_{l}^{2}
and so
\ddot{\mathfrak{c}}^{\prime;\prime\prime}_{l,1;l,1}=\ddot{\mathfrak{c}}^{\prime;\prime\prime}_{k,1;k,1}+\sigma_{l}^{2}=\ddot{\mathfrak{c}}_{k,1;k,2}+\sigma_{l}^{2}=\ddot{\mathfrak{c}}_{l,1;l,2}
.

•

Case:
f_{l}
is an BN layer.
\mathfrak{c}^{\prime;\prime\prime}_{l,1;l,1}
is obtained analogously to
\mathfrak{c}_{l,1;l,2}
via lemma
18
in stage 9, except that the components of
\chi_{d}
are now pairs of
e^{\prime}_{l^{\prime},1}-\widehat{e^{\prime}_{l^{\prime}}}
and
e^{\prime\prime}_{l^{\prime},1}-\widehat{e^{\prime\prime}_{l^{\prime}}}
instead of
e_{l^{\prime},1}-\widehat{e_{l^{\prime}}}
and
e_{l^{\prime},2}-\widehat{e_{l^{\prime}}}
(The
′
in the subscript has nothing to do with the
′
superscript.) This yields off-diagonal entries of zero for
\Sigma_{d}
but the same diagonal entries and hence the same
\hat{\Sigma}
. So we obtain the same value for
\mathfrak{c}^{\prime;\prime\prime}_{l,1;l,1}
as we did for
\mathfrak{c}_{l,1;l,2}
.

•

Case:
f_{l}
is an addition layer. We have
\mathfrak{c}^{\prime;\prime\prime}_{l,1;l,1}=\sum_{\kappa=1}^{K}w_{\kappa}^{2}\mathfrak{c}_{k[\kappa],1;k[\kappa],1}^{\prime;\prime\prime}+\sum_{\kappa\neq\kappa^{\prime}}w_{\kappa}w_{\kappa^{\prime}}\mathbb{E}_{e}\rho^{\prime}_{k[\kappa],1}\rho^{\prime\prime}_{k[\kappa^{\prime}],1}
. Analogously to stage 9,
\rho^{\prime}_{k[\kappa],1}
and
\rho^{\prime\prime}_{k[\kappa],1}
have inputs that originate from different big layers in
f
and only one of the two recursive expansions can hit an activation layer, so the latter sum is again zero. Hence,
\ddot{\mathfrak{c}}^{\prime;\prime\prime}_{l,1;l,1}=\sum_{\kappa=1}^{K}w_{\kappa}^{2}\ddot{\mathfrak{c}}^{\prime;\prime\prime}_{k[\kappa],1;k[\kappa],1}=\sum_{\kappa=1}^{K}w_{\kappa}^{2}\ddot{\mathfrak{c}}_{k[\kappa],1;k[\kappa],2}=\ddot{\mathfrak{c}}_{l,1;l,2}
as required.

•

Case:
f_{l}
is an activation layer. Again,
\mathfrak{c}^{\prime;\prime\prime}_{l,1;l,1}
is obtained analogously to
\mathfrak{c}_{l,1;l,2}
via lemma
18
in stage 9, except that the components of
\chi_{d}
are now pairs of
e^{\prime}_{l^{\prime},1}-\widehat{e^{\prime}_{l^{\prime}}}
and
e^{\prime\prime}_{l^{\prime},1}-\widehat{e^{\prime\prime}_{l^{\prime}}}
for

normed, pairs of

and
e^{\prime\prime}_{l^{\prime},1}
for
f_{l^{\prime}}
unnormed, as well as the

. Again,

is the same as before. So we obtain the same value for
\mathfrak{c}^{\prime;\prime\prime}_{l,1;l,1}
as we did for
\mathfrak{c}_{l,1;l,2}
.

We have

\displaystyle\lim_{\vec{\epsilon}}\lim_{B,N}\lim_{d_{\text{MF}}\text{ a.s.}}\frac{1}{d_{l}^{\text{MF}}}\mathbb{E}_{X}||f_{l,1}(X)||^{2}_{2}

as required. We have

Stage 12
: statement (
11.10
)

We proceed along the lines of stage 4. We begin with the case
l=m
. We have
\frac{1}{d_{l}^{\text{MF}}}\mathbb{E}_{X}\Tr(\mathcal{J}_{l,m,1}\mathrm{Cov}_{f_{m}}\mathcal{J}_{l,m,1}^{T})=\frac{1}{d_{m}^{\text{MF}}}\mathbb{E}_{X}\Tr((f_{m,1}(X)-\mathbb{E}_{X^{\prime}}f_{m,1}(X^{\prime}))(f_{m,1}(X)-\mathbb{E}_{X^{\prime}}f_{m,1}(X^{\prime}))^{T})=\frac{1}{d_{m}^{\text{MF}}}||\mathbb{S}_{X}f_{m,1}||^{2}_{2}
. So by stage 11, we have
\lim_{\vec{\epsilon}}\lim_{B,N}\lim_{d_{\text{MF}}\text{ a.s.}}\frac{1}{d_{l}^{\text{MF}}}\mathbb{E}_{X}\Tr(\mathcal{J}_{l,m}\mathrm{Cov}_{f_{m}}\mathcal{J}_{l,m}^{T})=\mathfrak{q}_{m}-\mathfrak{c}_{m}=\frac{\mathfrak{g}_{l}(\mathfrak{q}_{m}-\mathfrak{c}_{m})}{\mathfrak{g}_{m}}
as required.

For the remainder of this stage, assume
l>m
. Without loss of generality, we can also assume that
f_{m}
is a bottleneck for
f_{L}
in addition to being a bottleneck for
f_{l}
. Otherwise, we can simply apply the argument from this stage to the sub-architecture composed of

and its ancestors, which is a valid A-architecture, to obtain statement (
11.10
) for the pair

.

We have

\displaystyle\frac{1}{d_{l}^{\text{MF}}}\mathbb{E}_{X}\Tr(\mathcal{J}_{l,m,1}\mathrm{Cov}_{f_{m}}\mathcal{J}_{l,m,1}^{T})

\displaystyle=

\displaystyle\frac{1}{d_{l}^{\text{MF}}}\frac{1}{N^{2}}\sum_{n^{-},n^{+}=1}^{N}\Tr\Big(\mathcal{J}_{l,m,1}(X^{(n^{+})})(f_{m}(X^{(n^{-})})-\frac{1}{N}\sum_{n=1}^{N}f_{m}(X^{(n)}))^{T}...

\displaystyle...(f_{m}(X^{(n^{-})})-\frac{1}{N}\sum_{n=1}^{N}f_{m}(X^{(n)}))\mathcal{J}_{l,m,1}(X^{(n^{+})})^{T}\Big)

\displaystyle=

\displaystyle\frac{1}{d_{l}^{\text{MF}}}\frac{1}{N^{2}}\sum_{n^{-},n^{+}=1}^{N}||(f_{m}(X^{(n^{-})})-\frac{1}{N}\sum_{n=1}^{N}f_{m}(X^{(n)}))\mathcal{J}_{l,m,1}(X^{(n^{+})})^{T}||_{2}^{2}

\displaystyle=

\displaystyle\frac{1}{N^{2}}\sum_{n^{-},n^{+}=1}^{N}\overline{\Big((f_{m}(X^{(n^{-})})-\frac{1}{N}\sum_{n=1}^{N}f_{m}(X^{(n)}))\mathcal{J}_{l,m,1}(X^{(n^{+})})^{T}\Big)^{.2}}

Denote
(f_{m}(X^{(n^{-})})-\frac{1}{N}\sum_{n=1}^{N}f_{m}(X^{(n)}))\mathcal{J}_{l,m,1}(X^{(n^{+})})^{T}
by
p_{l,1}^{(n^{-},n^{+})}
. Then we have

\lim_{\vec{\epsilon}}\lim_{B,N}\lim_{d_{\text{MF}}\text{ a.s.}}\frac{1}{d_{l}^{\text{MF}}}\mathbb{E}_{X}\Tr(\mathcal{J}_{l,m,1}\mathrm{Cov}_{f_{m}}\mathcal{J}_{l,m,1}^{T})=\lim_{\vec{\epsilon}}\lim_{B,N}\frac{1}{N^{2}}\sum_{n^{-},n^{+}=1}^{N}\lim_{d_{\text{MF}}\text{ a.s.}}\overline{p_{l,1}^{(n^{-},n^{+})}.p_{l,1}^{(n^{-},n^{+})}}

As in stage 4, we conduct one induction per value of
m
to obtain
\lim_{d_{\text{MF}}\text{ a.s.}}\overline{p_{l,1}^{(n^{-},n^{+})}.p_{l,1}^{(n^{-},n^{+})}}
,
\lim_{B,N}\lim_{d_{\text{MF}}\text{ a.s.}}\overline{p_{l,1}^{(n^{-},n^{+})}.p_{l,1}^{(n^{-},n^{+})}}
and
\lim_{\vec{\epsilon}}\lim_{B,N}\lim_{d_{\text{MF}}\text{ a.s.}}\overline{p_{l,1}^{(n^{-},n^{+})}.p_{l,1}^{(n^{-},n^{+})}}
. Fix
m
for the rest of the stage. For now, also fix
n^{-}
and
n^{+}
.

Let’s look at the case
m>0
. We construct
F
as in stage 10, except that we construct the
N
-duplex of the
F
from stage 9 instead of the 2-duplex. We write
(F^{(1)},..,F^{(N)})
for that
N
-duplex as in stage 4, though we note that the
F^{(n)}
now themselves resemble a
B
-duplex and carry a batch index, as opposed to stage 4. As in stage 4, we use
\lambda
to denote a layer index that ranges from 1 to
m
.
\mathcal{G}
is constructed as in stage 10, except that
\mathsf{super1}
and
\mathsf{super2}
now range from 1 to
N
. We obtain control and distribution equality as before. By symmetry, we have that
\tilde{\mathfrak{m}}_{\lambda,1}^{(n)}=\tilde{\mathfrak{m}}_{\lambda,1}
,
\mathfrak{c}_{\lambda,1;\lambda,1}^{(n);(n)}=\mathfrak{c}_{\lambda,1;\lambda,1}
,
\mathfrak{c}_{\lambda,1;\lambda,2}^{(n);(n)}=\mathfrak{c}_{\lambda,1;\lambda,2}
and
\mathfrak{c}_{\lambda,1;\lambda,1}^{(n);(n^{\prime})}=\mathfrak{c}^{\prime;\prime\prime}_{\lambda,1;\lambda,1}
for

, where the right-hand sides stem from stages 9 and 10. By symmetry, we also have that those four limit quantities capture all combinations of batch indices, similar to stage 10. The limit of the right-hand sides as

is as in prior stages:
\ddot{\mathfrak{m}}_{\lambda,1}
,
\ddot{\mathfrak{c}}_{\lambda,1;\lambda,1}
,
\ddot{\mathfrak{c}}_{\lambda,1;\lambda,2}
and
\ddot{\mathfrak{c}}_{\lambda,1;\lambda,2}
respectively.

Next, we add layers
F^{\text{MN}}_{b}
as in stage 4 with
\rho^{\text{MN}}_{b}=\rho_{m,b}^{(n^{-})}-\frac{1}{N}\sum_{n=1}^{N}\rho^{(n)}_{m,b}
. Distribution equality follows as in stage 4 and control follows as for the addition layer in stage 9. As in stage 4, we have
\tilde{\mathfrak{m}}^{\text{MN}}_{1}=0
and
\mathfrak{c}^{\text{MN};\text{MN}}_{1;1}=(1-\frac{1}{N})(\mathfrak{c}_{m,1;m,1}-\mathfrak{c}_{m,1;m,1}^{\prime;\prime\prime})
. We also have

\mathfrak{c}^{\text{MN};\text{MN}}_{1;2}=\mathbb{E}_{e}(\rho_{m,1}^{(n-)}-\frac{1}{N}\sum_{n=1}^{N}\rho_{m,1}^{(n)})(\rho_{m,2}^{(n-)}-\frac{1}{N}\sum_{n=1}^{N}\rho_{m,2}^{(n)})=(1-\frac{1}{N})(\mathfrak{c}_{m,1;m,2}-\mathfrak{c}_{m,1;m,1}^{\prime;\prime\prime})

By symmetry, these three limit quantities cover all possible combinations of batch indices. When it comes to the joint distribution of
\rho^{\text{MN}}_{b}
and
\rho_{m,b}^{(n)}
, the cases

and

are distinct because in

for each

. Hence we consider both

and

. We obtain
\mathfrak{c}^{\text{MF};(n)}_{1;m,1}=(\mathbbm{1}_{n=n^{-}}-\frac{1}{N})(\mathfrak{c}_{m,1;m,1}-\mathfrak{c}_{m,1;m,1}^{\prime;\prime\prime})
as in stage 4 and

\mathfrak{c}^{\text{MF};(n)}_{1;m,2}=\mathbb{E}_{e}(\rho_{m,1}^{(n-)}-\frac{1}{N}\sum_{n^{\prime}=1}^{N}\rho_{m,1}^{(n^{\prime})})\rho_{m,2}^{(n)}=(\mathbbm{1}_{n=n^{-}}-\frac{1}{N})(\mathfrak{c}_{m,1;m,2}-\mathfrak{c}_{m,1;m,1}^{\prime;\prime\prime})

In terms of
\lim_{B,N}
quantities, we have
\ddot{\mathfrak{m}}^{\text{MN}}_{1}=0
,
\ddot{\mathfrak{c}}^{\text{MN};\text{MN}}_{1;1}=\ddot{\mathfrak{c}}_{m,1;m,1}-\ddot{\mathfrak{c}}_{m,1;m,2}
,
\ddot{\mathfrak{c}}^{\text{MF};(n)}_{1;m,1}=\mathbbm{1}_{n=n^{-}}(\ddot{\mathfrak{c}}_{m,1;m,1}-\ddot{\mathfrak{c}}_{m,1;m,2})
and
\ddot{\mathfrak{c}}^{\text{MN};\text{MN}}_{1;2}=\ddot{\mathfrak{c}}^{\text{MF};(n)}_{1;m,2}=0
.

After adding the
F^{\text{MN}}_{b}
, we also extend

beyond layers

as we did in stage 9. This corresponds to forward-propagating

beyond

. We denote all of

. Control follows as in stage 9.

Now let’s turn to the case

. In this scenario, we initialize our mean field architecture

to be

, usually shortened to

, as obtained by applying stage 9 to

and

.

Going forward, we treat the general case where

can be zero or non-zero. For each

, we want to add a layer to
F
for each

that represents

. We denote this layer by

. If

is not a BN layer, we do this as in stage 4, except that we now add
B
layers per

. Each of them depends only on other layers in

with the same batch index.

If
f_{l}
is a readin layer, the
F_{l,b}^{-}
are generated independently of each other and as
F_{l}^{-}
in stage 4. Distribution equality follows similarly to stage 4. We have
p_{l,b}^{(n^{-},n^{+})}=(x^{(n^{-},b)}-\frac{1}{N}\sum_{n=1}^{N}x^{(n,b)})W_{l}
and
f_{l,b}(X^{(n^{+})})=x^{(n^{+},b)}W_{l}
. Both are mean zero elementwise Gaussians. Further

\displaystyle\mathbb{E}_{W_{l}}p_{l,b}^{(n^{-},n^{+})}[i]p_{l,b^{\prime}}^{(n^{-},n^{+})}[i]

\displaystyle=

\displaystyle\sigma_{l}^{2}\overline{(x^{(n^{-},b)}-\frac{1}{N}\sum_{n=1}^{N}x^{(n,b)}).(x^{(n^{-},b^{\prime})}-\frac{1}{N}\sum_{n=1}^{N}x^{(n,b^{\prime})})}

\displaystyle=

\displaystyle\mathbbm{1}_{b=b^{\prime}}(1-\frac{1}{N})(q-c)\sigma_{l}^{2}

and

\displaystyle\mathbb{E}_{W_{l}}p_{l,b}^{(n^{-},n^{+})}[i]f_{l,b^{\prime}}(X^{(n^{+})})[i]

\displaystyle=

\displaystyle\sigma_{l}^{2}\overline{(x^{(n^{-},b)}-\frac{1}{N}\sum_{n=1}^{N}x^{(n,b)}).x^{(n^{+},b^{\prime})}}

\displaystyle=

\displaystyle\mathbbm{1}_{b=b^{\prime}}(\mathbbm{1}_{n^{-}=n^{+}}-\frac{1}{N})(q-c)\sigma_{l}^{2}

for all

. This corresponds to our choice of generator.

If
f_{l}
is a BN layer, we add elementwise layers

, each with the same width as any of the

. We set

\rho_{l,b}^{-}=\frac{\rho_{k,b}^{-}-\widehat{\rho_{k}^{-}}}{\sqrt{\nu_{l}^{+}}}-\frac{(\widehat{\rho_{k}^{-}\rho_{k}^{+}}-\widehat{\rho_{k}^{-}}\widehat{\rho_{k}^{+}})(\rho_{k,b}^{+}-\widehat{\rho_{k}^{+}})}{\sqrt{\nu_{l}^{+}}^{3}}

where
\nu_{l}^{+}=\mathbb{E}_{b}(\rho_{k,b}^{+}-\widehat{\rho_{k}^{+}})^{2}+\epsilon_{l}
as in stage 9. The inputs are those occurring in any of the
\rho_{k,b}^{-}
or
\rho_{k,b}^{+}
. It is easy to check that
F_{l,b}^{-}=\sum_{b^{\prime}=1}^{B}F_{k,b^{\prime}}^{-}J_{l,k,b,b^{\prime}}^{T}
, where
J_{l,k,b,b^{\prime}}
is the matrix obtained by evaluating
\frac{df_{l,b}(f_{k,1},..,f_{k,B})}{df_{k,b^{\prime}}}
at
(F_{k,1}^{+},..,F_{k,B}^{+})
. Hence, distribution equality holds.

So we are left to show limits and control. With regards to limits, we show that (i)
\tilde{\mathfrak{m}}^{-}_{l,1}
,
\mathfrak{c}^{-;-}_{l,1;l,1}
,
\mathfrak{c}^{-;-}_{l,1;l,2}
,
\mathfrak{c}^{-;+}_{l,1;l,1}
and
\mathfrak{c}^{-;+}_{l,1;l,2}
, which are valid because of background theorem
1
, are dependent on

and
